title: OpenHOI: Open-World Hand-Object Interaction Synthesis with Multimodal Large Language Model

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction contributions (Section 1) vs Section 4.3 Main Results and Abstract
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Introduction contributions bullet states: 'Our experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods by a large margin. Notably, OpenHOI generalizes robustly to unseen objects and open-vocabulary instructions, achieving strong compositional generalization across diverse scenarios.' But Section 4.3 Main Results states the opposite: 'Results in Tables 2 and 3 show marginal improvements in some metrics, though differences are within standard deviations reported by prior works. Detailed analysis suggests our approach has competitive performance but not a definitive advantage, especially given the relaxed unseen object definition in testing.' The Abstract likewise claims only 'competitive performance compared to recent methods.' The paper simultaneously asserts and disclaims its central superiority claim, which directly undermines the headline contribution.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, loss formulation (missing Equation 3 and undefined lambda weights)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper's equations jump from Eq. (2) to Eq. (4), so the combined training loss is never defined, yet the text says 'where the weights $\lambda_{\text{task}}, \lambda_{\text{aff}}$ are utilized to balance the different loss items.' No equation defining $L = \lambda_{\text{task}}L_{\text{task}} + \lambda_{\text{aff}}L_{\text{aff}}$ exists anywhere in the paper; the balancing-weights sentence is left referencing a removed/absent equation. This is a genuine methodological gap: the loss-balancing scheme that supervises the MLLM is described in prose but its defining formula (numbered 3) is missing.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.4 Ablation Study, Loss-guided Physical Refinement paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The ablation prose first concludes that the components contribute little: 'Excluding physical refinement losses causes occasional penetrations and minor temporal incoherence, but many sequences remain physically valid. The improvement from these components is thus incremental.' Two paragraphs later the same section asserts the opposite: 'Through direct optimization of these constraints via our loss-guidance framework, we achieve significant improvements in generating physically valid and temporally coherent hand-object interactions.' 'Incremental' vs 'significant improvements' are mutually exclusive claims about the same ablation, so the section contradicts itself.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.2, 'Training-free HOI Diffusion with Physical Refinement'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The method is repeatedly billed as 'training-free' and 'all achieved without additional training or distribution-shifting,' yet the refinement is implemented as iterative gradient descent on the sampling trajectory, which the paper itself acknowledges 'risks introducing artifacts and distribution shifts [49].' The resolution proposed (a 'Spherical Gaussian Constraint' borrowed from DSG) is asserted to 'preserve the original distribution, thus mitigating the distribution-shifting problem' without proof. The claim 'without ... distribution-shifting' sits in direct tension with the acknowledged risk that the same procedure 'risks introducing artifacts and distribution shifts,' leaving the training-free/distribution-preservation guarantee unsupported.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix C.6, Smooth Rate metric definition (Eq. 28)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines its new motion in-between metric as 'SmoothRate = dFID/dt, (28)' and states 'where dt is the derivative of time.' This is mathematically incoherent: dt is the differential of time (an infinitesimal increment), not 'the derivative of time.' dFID/dt is a rate of change of FID with respect to time, not a bounded 'smooth rate,' and the definition gives no computable operationalization for the values reported in Tables A8-A10 (e.g., 2.98 ± 0.43). As written the metric is undefined and its reported values cannot be reproduced or validated.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.3 Qualitative results vs Section 4.5 Failure cases
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Qualitative results paragraph claims: 'Experimental findings demonstrate physical realism and coherence of the generated sequences.' Section 4.5 immediately qualifies that 'Due to the accumulation of model errors, performance typically degrades after more than three consecutive actions (more than 450 frames)' and that the model cannot target a specific object in a scene. A blanket claim of 'physical realism and coherence' is contradicted by the paper's own documented failure modes (degradation on long-horizon sequences and poor spatial targeting), overgeneralizing from the small set of qualitative examples shown.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 3 vs Table 5 (ARCTIC seen-object FID and Diversity standard deviations)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The same 'Ours' ARCTIC seen-object results are reported with identical point estimates but different standard deviations across the two tables: FID 19.74±0.16 in Table 3 vs 19.74±0.35 in Table 5, and Diversity 2.65±0.03 in Table 3 vs 2.65±0.16 in Table 5. Unseen-object FID/Diversity and all other matched cells agree. The inconsistent error bars for identical numbers indicate a reporting discrepancy in the ablation table.

summary: Exhaustive lenient-mode verification of paper 8330 (OpenHOI). The manuscript was segmented into 53 typed snippets (22 sections, 16 tables, 8 display equations, 7 figure blocks) and routed through the specialist verifiers (math, text, statistical, vision, citation, cross-section consistency). The core methodology is largely internally coherent: the DDPM forward process (Eq. 5), classifier-free guidance (Eq. 7), posterior sampling mean/variance (Eq. 8, 23-26), the three refinement losses (Eqs. 9-11), and the DSG-style mixture update (Eqs. 12-14) were re-derived and check out. Web verification of the bibliography confirmed that the references flagged as potentially fabricated in the workspace ground truth — [3] DiffH2O (real SIGGRAPH Asia 2024 paper) and [5] 'Human-Object Interaction via Automatically Designed VLM-Guided Motion Policy' (real arXiv:2503.18349 / ICLR 2026 paper) — are in fact genuine publications, as are OakInk2 [53] and ShapeLLM/ReCon++ [34]. The most serious confirmed finding is a cross-section contradiction: the Introduction claims 'state-of-the-art performance, outperforming existing methods by a large margin,' while the Abstract and Section 4.3 explicitly disclaim a definitive advantage ('competitive performance but not a definitive advantage'), undermining the paper's central contribution claim (confidence 0.90). Additional confirmed issues: the MLLM training-loss equation is missing (equations jump 2→4) while the λ_task/λ_aff balancing weights it would define are still referenced in text; the ablation section calls the same components' effect both 'incremental' and 'significant improvements'; the 'training-free ... without distribution-shifting' claim is in tension with the paper's own acknowledgment that the gradient-descent refinement 'risks introducing artifacts and distribution shifts'; the Smooth Rate metric (Eq. 28) is defined as 'dFID/dt' with 'dt is the derivative of time,' which is mathematically incoherent; the qualitative section claims blanket 'physical realism and coherence' while the failure analysis documents degradation beyond three actions; and identical ARCTIC seen-object numbers carry different standard deviations in Table 3 vs Table 5. These findings, including one at confidence >= 0.85, yield a NEEDS_CORRECTION verdict.
